full_target:
A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
correction.

Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.
proof:
Scope and original data. Work with exactly the selected interpretation and H: n,m≥1, X=ℝ^n and V=ℝ^m with Euclidean norms, jointly C∞ u:X×(0,∞)→V, a fixed q∈V with ‖q‖=1, ‖u(x,t)‖=1 everywhere, ∀(x,t)∃a∈ℝ such that u_tt−Σ_j u_jj=a u, and ∀0<s<t∃ compact C⊂X with u=q off C throughout [s,t]. There is no regularity assumption on the scalar witnesses. The spatial sum is over Fin n, so it is the Frobenius square and componentwise Laplacian of the original statement. Volume is Euclidean Lebesgue measure. The density is e=‖u_t‖²+Σ_j‖u_j‖² with no factor 1/2. E is its actual spatial integral.

Representation, used in all steps. Put Z=X×ℝ and Ω={(x,r):r>0}, an open set. Choose any total representative U:Z→V agreeing with u on Ω, assigning for example 0 outside Ω. This introduces no regularity outside Ω: the hypothesis is ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ U Ω. Here ∞ is the C∞ order, not analytic order ω. Set τ=(0,1), σ_j=(e_j,0), where e_j is the jth Euclidean coordinate vector. For a total field F and constant v define D_vF(z)=(fderiv ℝ F z)v. Use U_t=D_τU, U_j=D_σjU, U_tt=D_τU_t, U_jj=D_σjU_j on Ω. These are the original partial derivatives. Indeed affine curves r↦(x,r) and h↦(x+h e_j,r) have the indicated constant derivatives (their linear approximation has identically zero remainder), and B013 identifies directional and ordinary derivatives. At an interior point there is no within-domain boundary issue. All formulas are independent of the arbitrary representative: agreement on an open neighborhood implies equality of derivatives by B010; equality holds at every point of that same open set, so induction gives equality of every iterated derivative field there.

Complete regularity reduction shared by R001–R004. Apply B004 on Ω to U: U is differentiable there and its derivative map is C∞ there. Apply B005 to that derivative map and the constant field v to see that D_vU is C∞. Iterating proves the same for every finite ordered constant-direction derivative used below. Constants are smooth from their zero derivatives. B009 proves smoothness of inner products; identify ‖F‖²=⟪F,F⟫. B014 gives smoothness of finite sums, with an extra singleton term if necessary to include the time contribution. Restricting to affine spatial or time sections is justified by B019 with S=X or an interval, T=Ω, and the affine inclusion; its MapsTo premise is r>0. Thus the sections and all displayed derivative products are continuous, and the required spatial sections are differentiable.

The mixed-derivative bridge must be made explicit. The derivative map A=fderiv ℝ U is differentiable at each z∈Ω by B004 and openness. In B007 take b≡v. Db=0, hence D_w(D_vU)(z)=(fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ U) z) w v. C∞ gives C² at z; B006 then yields D_wD_vU=D_vD_wU. In particular D_τU_j=D_σjU_t. This uses only local smoothness inside Ω.

R001, tangency and orthogonal acceleration. At fixed z∈Ω apply B008 to f=g=U and v=τ. Real inner-product symmetry gives D_τ‖U‖²=2⟪U,U_t⟫. The unit constraint is an identity with constant 1 on the open set Ω. B010 makes its derivative zero, so ⟪U,U_t⟫=0. At this point alone eliminate the original existential scalar: choose a with U_tt−Σ_jU_jj=a U. Bilinearity and symmetry give ⟪U_t,U_tt−Σ_jU_jj⟫=a⟪U_t,U⟫=0. This proves N001 everywhere positive. No scalar is selected globally or differentiated. The optional explicit formula for a in the supplied proof is unnecessary and is omitted.

R002, common support, regularity and integrability. Fix arbitrary t₀>0. Put s=t₀/2 and b=3t₀/2, so 0<s<t₀<b, and choose the original compact support set C for [s,b]. Euclidean compact C is closed and Borel measurable. The set A=(X\C)×(s,b) is open and U=q on A. At every point of A, B010 compares U with the constant q, yielding DU=0. The same reasoning applies at every point of A to each already-zero derivative field; induction shows all positive-order derivatives of U vanish there. In particular U_t,U_j,U_tt,U_jj,D_σjU_t vanish for x∉C and r∈(s,b). Therefore e, its time derivative, and each real product
T=⟪U_t,U_tt⟫, A_j=⟪U_j,D_σjU_t⟫, B_j=⟪U_t,U_jj⟫, H_j=⟪U_t,U_j⟫
vanish there too. These fields are smooth by the shared calculus reduction. The same compact C works for every r in the open interval; nothing about derivatives at s or b is asserted.

For any such scalar section h at an interior time, continuity on X implies continuity on C. B003 gives IntegrableOn h C volume; B012 gives integrability of C.indicator h, which equals h pointwise because h vanishes outside C. Thus e and every listed product are integrable, including the undifferentiated H_j required by B002. The same applies to e_t: e is already smooth, so B004/B005 make its time-direction derivative smooth; B013 identifies it with the ordinary time derivative. The explicit product formula is derived separately in R003. There is no assumption that U itself has compact support. If C is empty, all these scalar sections are zero and the argument still applies.

R003, differentiation of the actual integral. Apply B008 with both factors U_t and direction τ, and separately with both factors U_j and direction τ. Apply B013 to the time curves and B015 to the finitely many summands, including the extra time summand. Mixed-partial symmetry established above gives, for every x and r>0,
G(r,x):=∂_r e(x,r)=2T(x,r)+2Σ_j A_j(x,r).
This is precisely the density derivative with the original normalization. It is jointly continuous on Ω, and e and G have spatial support in C for all r∈(s,b), by R002.

Choose η=t₀/4>0 and K=[t₀−η,t₀+η]⊂(s,b). The product C×K is compact. Apply B011 to the continuous scalar field (x,r)↦G(r,x) on C×K to obtain B₀ with |G(r,x)|≤B₀ there; take B=max(B₀,0). Put β(x)=C.indicator(fun _=>B)(x). Its constant restriction to C is continuous, so B003 and B012 give Integrable β volume. This uses only finite measure on compact sets, already supplied by the Lebesgue specialization of B003. For every x∈C and r∈(t₀−η,t₀+η) the compact bound gives |G(r,x)|≤β(x). For x∉C, G(r,x)=0=β(x). Thus there is one pointwise bound for all x and all times in that common open interval, which supplies the stronger uniform almost-everywhere premise of B001.

Apply B001 with F(r,x)=e(x,r), derivative field G, s'=(t₀−η,t₀+η), spatial bound β, measured space X, scalar and codomain ℝ. The neighborhood premise follows from η>0. For r near t₀, spatial e sections are continuous, hence a.e. strongly measurable (alternatively their R002 integrability gives this immediately). R002 gives integrability of F(t₀,·). The G(t₀,·) section is continuous and compactly supported, hence integrable by the same B003/B012 argument and therefore a.e. strongly measurable. The bound and its integrability were just proved. Finally the ordinary time derivative premise holds for every x and r∈s' by the displayed product/sum calculation, so also almost everywhere with a single spatial full-measure set. All seven premises of B001 have now been checked. It returns
HasDerivAt (r↦∫_X e(x,r)dx) (∫_X G(t₀,x)dx) t₀
and integrability of G(t₀,·). The total representative of E agrees with the actual finite energy integral on all positive times. Only that open neighborhood is used. Thus N003 asserts integrability of e(·,t) and this derivative formula for every t>0. No assertion at time zero or global time-uniform bound has entered.

R004, integration by parts. At fixed t₀>0 and j choose f(x)=U_t(x,t₀), g(x)=U_j(x,t₀) and v=e_j. The shared regularity argument and B019 give global smoothness of these spatial sections, so they are differentiable at every spatial point, in particular on each other's topological supports. Their spatial directional derivatives are D_σjU_t and U_jj, respectively: identify them along the affine coordinate curves using B013 and uniqueness of ordinary derivatives. All three scalar products in B002 are integrable by R002, including ⟪f,g⟫=H_j. B002 gives
∫_X B_j(x,t₀)dx = −∫_X ⟪D_σjU_t,U_j⟫(x,t₀)dx.
Real inner-product symmetry identifies the last integrand with A_j. Equivalently ∫A_j=−∫B_j. This is the supplied compact-support integration-by-parts step, using Mathlib's proved finite-dimensional bilinear theorem instead of repeating its internal one-dimensional IBP and Fubini proof. There is no boundary regularity assumption on C and no surface term. This proves N004 for every j and t₀.

R005, finite cancellation and conclusion. Every product and finite sum involved is integrable by N002. B018 and B017 split the density derivative integral, and B016 interchanges the finite spatial sums with the integrals:
∫G(t₀,x)dx=2∫T+2Σ_j∫A_j
=2∫T−2Σ_j∫B_j.
For completeness, the minus in the second equality is ordinary finite algebra applied to N004; no infinite-series passage occurs. By pointwise bilinearity Σ_jB_j=⟪U_t,Σ_jU_jj⟫. N001 says pointwise that T=Σ_jB_j. Pointwise equality and B016 give ∫T=Σ_j∫B_j, so the displayed derivative is zero. Consequently N003 gives HasDerivAt E 0 t₀, hence differentiability and E'(t₀)=0. Since t₀>0 was arbitrary and the integrability argument also holds at every such time, this is precisely P. The optional conclusion that E is constant follows from the ordinary mean value theorem on any compact positive-time interval, but is not required to establish the selected derivative target and is not used as a foundation.

Dependency and source accounting. B001–B019 are specializations of actual Mathlib declarations, with their mathematical premises retained and proof bodies to be checked after this complete route is selected. Each is class 1/adapted, not a class-3 bundle mislabeled as one unchanged imported theorem. New local derivations are the explicit R001–R005 arguments above: compact support by locality, compact bounds and indicator domination, mixed derivative identification by evaluation and symmetry, and the final cancellation. They are downstream NL0 steps and make no additional external assumptions. Smooth constants and affine inclusions have zero derivative remainders; openness allows ordinary local derivatives. Elementary finite algebra, equality substitution, compact product/closedness facts in finite-dimensional Euclidean topology, and the basic definition-level implications from smoothness to continuity/differentiability are used with the conditions stated above. The analytic operations are all explicitly registered. Local source inspection is evidence of availability, not independent mathematical review or successful kernel checking. No class 4, textbook axiom, source-qualified fallback or claim of completed unconditional Lean formalization is made in this draft.

import Mathlib
open MeasureTheory Set Filter
open scoped Topology ContDiff BigOperators

dependencies.statement: For every n≥0, real F,G:ℝ→ℝ^n→ℝ, t₀, neighborhood s of t₀, and real spatial bound b, assume: F(t,·) is a.e. strongly measurable for t near t₀; F(t₀,·) is integrable; G(t₀,·) is a.e. strongly measurable; for a.e. x, all t∈s satisfy |G(t,x)|≤b(x) and the ordinary time derivative of F(·,x) at t equals G(t,x); and b is integrable. Then G(t₀,·) is integrable and t↦∫F(t,x)dx has derivative ∫G(t₀,x)dx at t₀.

origin.revision: task-selected frozen Mathlib checkout; exact declaration checked by the native preparation

lean.type:
∀ (n : ℕ) (F G : ℝ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ) (t₀ : ℝ) (s : Set ℝ) (b : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ),
s ∈ 𝓝 t₀ →
(∀ᶠ t in 𝓝 t₀, AEStronglyMeasurable (F t) volume) →
Integrable (F t₀) volume →
AEStronglyMeasurable (G t₀) volume →
(∀ᵐ x ∂volume, ∀ t ∈ s, ‖G t x‖ ≤ b x) →
Integrable b volume →
(∀ᵐ x ∂volume, ∀ t ∈ s, HasDerivAt (fun r => F r x) (G t x) t) →
Integrable (G t₀) volume ∧ HasDerivAt (fun t => ∫ x, F t x) (∫ x, G t₀ x) t₀
lean.proof:
intro n F G t₀ s b hs hF_meas hF_int hG_meas h_bound hb_int h_diff
exact hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le
  (𝕜 := ℝ) (μ := volume) (F := F) (F' := G) (x₀ := t₀) (s := s) (bound := b)
  hs hF_meas hF_int hG_meas h_bound hb_int h_diff

dependencies.justification: Set scalar and codomain to ℝ, spatial measured type to EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), measure to volume; preserve all seven hypotheses and both conclusions. This is a specialization of the named proved declaration, not a claim of native whole-type identity.

dependencies.statement: For every n,m≥0 and f,g:ℝ^n→ℝ^m and v∈ℝ^n, if ⟪D_v f,g⟫, ⟪f,D_v g⟫ and ⟪f,g⟫ are integrable, f is differentiable on the topological support of g, and g is differentiable on that of f, then ∫⟪f,D_v g⟫=−∫⟪D_v f,g⟫. D_v is the Fréchet derivative evaluated at v; norms and volume are Euclidean.

origin.revision: task-selected frozen Mathlib checkout; exact declaration checked by the native preparation

lean.type:
∀ (n m : ℕ) (f g : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) (v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)),
Integrable (fun x => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ f x v) (g x)) volume →
Integrable (fun x => inner ℝ (f x) (fderiv ℝ g x v)) volume →
Integrable (fun x => inner ℝ (f x) (g x)) volume →
(∀ x ∈ tsupport g, DifferentiableAt ℝ f x) →
(∀ x ∈ tsupport f, DifferentiableAt ℝ g x) →
(∫ x, inner ℝ (f x) (fderiv ℝ g x v)) = -(∫ x, inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ f x v) (g x))
lean.proof:
have yui_nested_41461d4beddbb5390efa_0001  : (∀ (m : ℕ) (a b : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)), (innerSL ℝ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m) →L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m) →L[ℝ] ℝ) a b = inner ℝ a b) := by
  intro m a b
  rfl
have yui_nested_41461d4beddbb5390efa_0002  : (∀ (n m : ℕ) (a b : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)), Integrable (fun x => inner ℝ (a x) (b x)) volume → Integrable (fun x => (innerSL ℝ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m) →L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m) →L[ℝ] ℝ) (a x) (b x)) volume) := by
  intro n m a b h
  simpa only [yui_nested_41461d4beddbb5390efa_0001] using h
have yui_nested_41461d4beddbb5390efa_0003  : (∀ (n m : ℕ) (a b : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)), (∫ x, (innerSL ℝ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m) →L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m) →L[ℝ] ℝ) (a x) (b x)) = ∫ x, inner ℝ (a x) (b x)) := by
  intro n m a b
  exact congrArg (fun h : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ => ∫ x, h x) (funext (fun x => yui_nested_41461d4beddbb5390efa_0001 m (a x) (b x)))
intro n m f g v hf'g hfg' hfg hf hg
have H := integral_bilinear_fderiv_right_eq_neg_left_of_integrable
    (μ := (volume : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))))
    (f := f) (g := g) (v := v)
    (B := (innerSL ℝ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m) →L[ℝ]
      EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m) →L[ℝ] ℝ))
    (yui_nested_41461d4beddbb5390efa_0002 n m (fun x => fderiv ℝ f x v) g hf'g)
    (yui_nested_41461d4beddbb5390efa_0002 n m f (fun x => fderiv ℝ g x v) hfg')
    (yui_nested_41461d4beddbb5390efa_0002 n m f g hfg)
    hf hg
exact (yui_nested_41461d4beddbb5390efa_0003 n m f (fun x => fderiv ℝ g x v)).symm.trans
  (H.trans (congrArg Neg.neg (yui_nested_41461d4beddbb5390efa_0003 n m (fun x => fderiv ℝ f x v) g)))

dependencies.justification: Specialize the bilinear form to innerSL ℝ and Haar measure to Lebesgue volume on finite-dimensional Euclidean space. Keep all three integrability and both differentiability premises; innerSL_apply_apply is the value adapter. dependencies.statement: For real normed spaces E,F and f:E→F which is C² at z, its second Fréchet derivative is symmetric: for every v,w∈E, D(Df)(z)[v][w]=D(Df)(z)[w][v].

lean.type: ∀ (E F : Type) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F], ∀ (f : E → F) (z : E), ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f z → ∀ v w : E, fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) z v w = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) z w v
lean.proof:
intro E F _ _ _ _ f z hf
have hs : IsSymmSndFDerivAt ℝ f z :=
  hf.isSymmSndFDerivAt (by simp)
change ∀ v w : E, fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) z v w = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) z w v at hs
exact hs

propositions.statement: Let n,m≥1 be integers, X=ℝ^n and V=ℝ^m with their Euclidean structures, and u:X×(0,∞)→V jointly C∞. Let q∈V be fixed with ‖q‖=1. For r>0 write u_t=∂_t u, u_j=∂_{x_j}u, u_tt=∂²_tu, u_jj=∂²_{x_j}u, Δ_xu=Σ_{j=1}^n u_jj, e(x,r)=‖u_t(x,r)‖²+Σ_j‖u_j(x,r)‖² and E(r)=∫_X e(x,r)dx, using Lebesgue measure and Frobenius gradient square.
For every x∈ℝ^n and t>0, ‖u(x,t)‖=1 and there exists a real scalar a such that u_tt(x,t)−Σ_{j=1}^n u_jj(x,t)=a u(x,t). No regularity is assumed for any selection of these pointwise scalar witnesses.
For every pair of real times 0<s<t, there is a compact set C⊂ℝ^n such that for every x∉C and every r∈[s,t], u(x,r)=q, where q is the same fixed unit vector at all points and times.

For every jointly smooth sphere-valued map u:ℝ^n×(0,∞)→ℝ^m with n,m≥1 and pointwise normal acceleration u_tt−Σ_j u_jj=a u for a real pointwise witness a, at every x∈ℝ^n and t>0 one has ⟪u,u_t⟫=0 and ⟪u_t,u_tt−Σ_j u_jj⟫=0. No regularity of the scalar witnesses is needed.

Let n,m≥1 and let u:ℝ^n×(0,∞)→ℝ^m be jointly smooth and equal to a fixed q outside a common compact spatial set on each closed positive-time slab. Define u_t,u_j,u_tt,u_jj, e=‖u_t‖²+Σ_j‖u_j‖² and the products T=⟪u_t,u_tt⟫, A_j=⟪u_j,∂_{x_j}u_t⟫, B_j=⟪u_t,u_jj⟫ and H_j=⟪u_t,u_j⟫. These fields and ∂_t e are jointly smooth at positive times. For every t₀>0 there is a compact C⊂ℝ^n such that all positive-order derivatives of u and all these scalar fields vanish for x∉C and r∈(t₀/2,3t₀/2). Their spatial sections there are continuous, compactly supported and Lebesgue integrable. Also ∂_t u_j=∂_{x_j}u_t everywhere at positive times.

For n,m≥1 and a jointly smooth u:ℝ^n×(0,∞)→ℝ^m equal to a fixed q outside a common compact spatial set on every closed positive-time slab, put e=‖u_t‖²+Σ_j‖u_j‖² and E(t)=∫_{ℝ^n}e(x,t)dx. For every t>0 the density is integrable and E has ordinary derivative ∫_{ℝ^n}(2⟪u_t,u_tt⟫+2Σ_j⟪u_j,∂_{x_j}u_t⟫)(x,t)dx at t. The derivative integrand and each summand are integrable. This derivative assertion is local on (0,∞), independent of any extension to nonpositive times.

For n,m≥1 and a jointly smooth u:ℝ^n×(0,∞)→ℝ^m equal to a fixed q outside a common compact spatial set on every closed positive-time slab, for every t>0 and j∈{1,…,n}, both real products in the identity ∫_{ℝ^n}⟪u_j,∂_{x_j}u_t⟫(x,t)dx=−∫_{ℝ^n}⟪u_t,u_jj⟫(x,t)dx are integrable and the identity holds.

A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
correction.

Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.
